CVE-2026-112913.title: filelock: ReadWriteLock on Windows acts on SQLite side files another local user places beside its database

CVE-2026-98994.title: statmount: read the parent of an unmounted mount under mount_lock
CVE-2026-98994.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

statmount: read the parent of an unmounted mount under mount_lock

statmount_mnt_basic() reads the ids of the parent through m->mnt_parent
with namespace_sem held for reading. That's fine for a mount that is
in a namespace. Everything above it is pinned by that namespace.

STATMOUNT_BY_FD also accepts a file descriptor on a mount that has
been unmounted on purpose and that only the file descriptor keeps alive.
If that mount stayed attached to its parent when it was unmounted the
parent is unmounted as well and nothing pins it for the child.

The final mntput() unmounts the children under mount_lock alone and
frees the parent afterwards. Concurrently, statmount_mnt_basic() reads
m->mnt_parent twice while that can happen and can easily dereference a
mount that's already gone.

Read the parent of an unmounted mount under mount_lock. The parent
can't be put while it is held and both ids come from the same mount.…

CVE-2026-99427.title: smb: client: fix OOB last_entry pointer from unbounded LastNameOffset
CVE-2026-99427.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: fix OOB last_entry pointer from unbounded LastNameOffset

CIFSFindFirst() and CIFSFindNext() locate the last entry of a
TRANS2_FIND_FIRST2 or TRANS2_FIND_NEXT2 response by adding the
LastNameOffset of the response parameters to the start of the data
area, and store the result in psrch_inf->last_entry. MS-CIFS 2.2.6.2.2
defines that offset as the offset of the entry's file name; the client
follows the reading of NT and Samba servers, which point it at the
entry. LastNameOffset is only checked against CIFSMaxBufSize, which
says nothing about the response actually received: validate_t2() lets
the data area start up to 1024 bytes into the buffer, and SendReceive()

CVE-2026-99742.title: mm/mempolicy: charge shared policy nodes
CVE-2026-99742.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/mempolicy: charge shared policy nodes

Any local user can bypass memory.max with mbind() on a tmpfs file, and
allocate unbounded kernel memory.

mbind() sets a NUMA memory policy for a range of a mapping. If the
mapping is of a shmem and friends, the kernel also stores the policy on
the inode, in a tree with one entry per range of the file.

Each mbind() on a single page of a mapping can add one shared policy node
(struct sp_node) and one struct mempolicy to that tree. They outlive the
mapping and stay around until the inode is destroyed. The tree is not
bounded by the file size, so the file can be empty.

slab cache does that for all of its objects if it is created with
SLAB_ACCOUNT. numa_policy_init() creates the slab caches for both
structs without SLAB_ACCOUNT, so they are not charged to any cgroup.
